chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not befitting for the Muslim man to establish brotherhood with the immoral, nor the fool, nor the liar.

key_terms.الأحمق: The ahmaq — the fool, one lacking sound judgment; dangerous as a companion because well-intentioned foolishness can cause harm
key_terms.الفاجر: The fajir — one who openly transgresses moral and religious boundaries; the dissolute or immoral person
key_terms.الكذاب: The kadhdhab — the habitual, compulsive liar; the intensified form (fa''al) indicates someone defined by their lying
key_terms.يواخي: To establish mu'akha (brotherhood bond); a formal or deep bond of brotherhood beyond ordinary friendship

ai.seo_question: Who should a Muslim avoid befriending according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns that a Muslim should not form close brotherly bonds with three types of people: the morally corrupt (fajir), the fool (ahmaq), and the habitual liar (kadhdhab). This teaching reflects a broader Islamic principle that a person's character is shaped by their companions, and that friendship with those of poor character risks corrupting one's own faith and morals. The early Muslim community understood this as guidance for protecting the integrity of one's religious life and social circle.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Yusuf, from Muyassar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is not befitting for the Muslim man that he establishes brotherhood with an immoral, nor an idiot, nor a liar’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Yusuf from Maysir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
It is not proper for a Muslim man to become friends with an indecent, an idiot and a liar.”
